item.title: Hyogo Prefectural Museum of Art: Tadao Ando on the Waterfront — Guide
item.description: The Hyogo Prefectural Museum of Art is the largest art museum in western Japan and as much an architectural destination as an art one: its building, completed in 2002 by Tadao Ando, is a monumental composition of raw concrete, glass volumes and open external stairways stepping down to the Kobe waterfront, built as part of the city’s cultural recovery after the 1995 Great Hanshin earthquake. The collection spans modern Japanese and Western sculpture, prints and painting, and even without a ticket the terraces, stairways and sea-facing spaces are free to explore.

item.title: Minato Mirai 21 Guide: Landmark Tower, Views & Access
item.description: Minato Mirai 21 (“Future Port”) is Yokohama’s glittering waterfront district and one of the Tokyo area’s best night-out destinations. Built on reclaimed harbour land, this sleek, futuristic quarter pairs the Landmark Tower — long Japan’s tallest building, with a 69th-floor Sky Garden observatory — with the giant Cosmo Clock 21 Ferris wheel, the historic Red Brick Warehouse, museums, malls and a romantic, illuminated bayfront promenade. Easy to reach and dazzling after dark, it’s the modern face of Yokohama and a perfect complement to the city’s Chinatown and old port heritage.

item.title: Osaka Bay Guide: Kaiyukan, the Ferris Wheel & Sakurajima
item.description: West of the city centre, Osaka Bay opens the metropolis to the sea — a breezy waterfront of attractions, harbour views, and big-sky sunsets that makes a refreshing change from the neon canyons of Minami. Here you’ll find the giant Tempozan Ferris wheel, the superb Kaiyukan aquarium, sightseeing cruises, and, across the water on Sakurajima, Universal Studios Japan. It’s family territory and a great spot to watch the sun sink over the harbour.
